messages.subject: element_text(lineheight = ... on multiline math expressions
parts:
Is there a ggplot alternative to using plotmath epression(atop( to get multiline axis titles?

Simply using allows lineheight control but looks horrible. Using expression(atop( looks nicer but has large in built lineheight that can't be changed with ggplot themes.

library(ggplot2)

# Multi line expression
qplot(x = 1, y = 1, xlab = expression(atop("line1", ~line^2)))

# Adjust line height to no avail
qplot(x = 1, y = 1, xlab = expression(atop("line1", ~line^2))) +
theme(axis.title.x = element_text(lineheight = 0.5, debug = TRUE))

# Insert extra line break with allows control of that line height
qplot(x = 1, y = 1, xlab = expression(atop("line1 ", ~line^2))) +
theme(axis.title.x = element_text(lineheight = 0.5, debug = TRUE))

# But we can't control the line break created by atop
qplot(x = 1, y = 1, xlab = expression(atop("line1 ", ~line^2))) +
theme(axis.title.x = element_text(lineheight = 0.00001, debug = TRUE))

# Removing atop causes other issues with centering...
qplot(x = 1, y = 1, xlab = expression("line1 " ~line^2)) +
theme(axis.title.x = element_text(lineheight = 1, debug = TRUE))

Would this require arrange two searate text grobs for each line? Or is there a simpler way?
